topic: EXP-562 tldr batch verification (PRED-TIER-2, PRED-R003, PRED-R004, W017, W019, W024)
change_summary: Decider commit 8d9af3a added tldr field to 6 prediction entries per EXP-562. Verify tldr ↔ detail_reasoning alignment and additive-only constraint.
our_argument_summary: Six TLDR fields were added to predictions.json: three recycled-class entries (PRED-TIER-2 gravity pulse, PRED-R003 NMP 141-146E by 2031, PRED-R004 NMP drift ratio ≥2.0× through 2028), one standard_physics (W017 Schumann ≥7.85 Hz under high solar wind), and two falsified (W019 NMP poleward dominance, W024 Polaris elevation >55°N excess). Each TLDR is a 2-3 sentence summary of the existing detail_reasoning, intended as progressive-disclosure UX for the predictions tab. The decider/analyst frame this as verification-class (no new argument, no verdict change, additive-only) which is honest given the patch shape.

per_prediction_assessment.notes: TLDR correctly identifies (a) restatement of WIN-011, (b) Mohe 1997 data → 29-year predates (1997 + 29 = 2026 ✓ arithmetic), (c) Van Camp et al. (2001) null-result with four superconducting gravimeters, (d) framing as zero-new-content. WIN-011 verdict spot-check: 'Not Demonstrated' ✓ matches detail_reasoning. The recycled verdict is well-supported.

TLDR correctly identifies (a) NMP 141-146°E by 2031 as IGRF/WMM extrapolation, (b) absence of dome-specific derivation, (c) the both-models-or-neither symmetry that makes this unfalsifiable in the dome's favor. WIN-043 verdict spot-check: 'Std Model Explains' ✓ matches detail_reasoning. The recycled verdict is well-supported.

TLDR correctly identifies (a) extension of WIN-043 to 2028, (b) arithmetic-from-NOAA framing, (c) no dome-vs-standard distinction. Consistent with PRED-R003 framing on the same WIN. Recycled verdict well-supported.

TLDR correctly identifies (a) solar wind → ionospheric compression → Schumann frequency shift as textbook M-I coupling, (b) 7.85 Hz sits inside the 7.7-8.0 Hz normal diurnal band (math check: 7.7 < 7.85 < 8.0 ✓), (c) data predates registration (2026-03-12). The standard_physics verdict is well-supported.

TLDR correctly identifies (a) core-mantle boundary flux dynamics as the standard-physics explanation, (b) author self-status REFINED ↔ database confirms author_status=refined ✓, (c) WIN-043 absorbs the trajectory. One observation: the TLDR mentions the dome's REFINED status without explicitly tagging our verdict as falsified. For a non-science reader, the verdict label rendered alongside the panel carries that signal — the TLDR's conclusion (no new test) is consistent with either recycled or falsified, so this is not a factual error. Imprecision-without-mislead per curmudgeon.md TLDR guidance → not flagging as a hole.

TLDR correctly identifies (a) the >55°N prediction, (b) author self-classification FALSIFIED ↔ database confirms author_status=falsified ✓, (c) WIN-065 supporting context (+0.27° at 35.9°N within 0.74° refraction/instrument offset). WIN-065 verdict spot-check: 'Refuted by Data' ✓ matches detail_reasoning. The >55°N prediction vs 35.9°N measurement scale-mismatch is fine because the author has independently self-classified as FALSIFIED — the WIN-065 reference is supporting context, not the load-bearing argument. The falsified verdict is well-supported. Note: data_predates_registration=false on this entry (the only one in the batch) — TLDR correctly omits any predates-registration claim, preserving accuracy.

kernel_of_truth.description: EXP-562 (monitor/analyst/expansions/EXP-562.json) is correctly scoped as verification-class progressive-disclosure UX backfill. The patch_type 'data_field_addition' with action='set_field' on a previously-absent tldr field is genuinely additive — verified by inspection of commit 8d9af3a where the only changes to data/predictions.json are six +tldr lines and six trailing-comma additions on the preceding detail_reasoning lines (12 insertions, 6 deletions, all mechanical). The TLDRs themselves are faithful 2-3 sentence summaries of detail_reasoning prose that was curmudgeon-reviewed in prior cycles when the verdicts landed (PRED-batch-2026-04-10 / -04-18 reviews per W019 verdict_history). The analyst's anticipated_objection §1 in EXP-562.json — 'verification-class is honest here; deep-attack would burn an Opus curmudgeon run on summary-of-prior-work content' — is correct.

deeper_analysis: Adversarial lens applied to each TLDR: (1) factual content: all six TLDRs accurately paraphrase their detail_reasoning. Specific cross-checks: 1997+29=2026 (PRED-TIER-2 ✓), 7.7<7.85<8.0 Hz (W017 ✓), 141-146°E by 2031 (PRED-R003, taken verbatim from claim ✓), ≥2.0× through 2028 (PRED-R004 ✓). (2) Citation integrity: WIN-011 verdict='Not Demonstrated' ✓, WIN-043 verdict='Std Model Explains' ✓, WIN-065 verdict='Refuted by Data' ✓ — all referenced WINs exist with the verdicts the detail_reasoning (and TLDR by reference) claim. Van Camp et al. (2001) and Wang et al. (2000) appear in PRED-TIER-2's detail_reasoning and are correctly summarized in the TLDR without misattribution. (3) Cross-WIN consistency: PRED-TIER-2/R003/R004 reference WIN-011/043 verdicts that are still current; W019/W024 reference falsified self-classification matching author_status fields in predictions.json ✓. (4) Smart-defender attack on the W019 TLDR: a defender could argue we soften by saying 'author marked REFINED' without flagging that we count this falsified — but the panel-level verdict label (rendered alongside the TLDR in the UX) carries our verdict, and the TLDR's conclusion 'adds no new test' is consistent with both recycled and falsified buckets, so no factual mislead. Per curmudgeon.md TLDR guidance ('only flag if the simplification is actually wrong, not just imprecise'), this is below threshold for a hole. (5) Additive-only verification: commit 8d9af3a diff confirms exactly six +tldr field additions in data/predictions.json, with the only collateral changes being six trailing commas on adjacent detail_reasoning lines (mechanical, JSON syntax). No detail_reasoning, our_verdict, claim, classification, or other field touched. The EXP-562 anticipated_objection about 'pure progressive-disclosure UX backfill' is corroborated by the diff. (6) Sequencing note for the decider: EXP-562's summary_for_decider correctly flags that 53 entries remain without TLDR after this batch; analyst-baby may template-handle the standard_physics/recycled cohort in subsequent batches per Mode 1b conventions. This is the right move — the same template will scale, the per-entry adversarial judgment is what we exercised here. No carry-over open holes; ISS-2477 remains partially-open (53 of 70 still uncovered).
